FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Driving demands health and sound judgment, with regular eye checks, lenses always worn, and no dark tints at night [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Drivers must read side motion through peripheral sight plus judge distances for lane position and hazard response [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Hearing warns of horns, sirens, and unseen cars, and fading hearing needs testing since the deaf compensate visually [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Fatigue dulls vision and slows decisions, so trips start rested with 7 to 9 hours of sleep, stops every 100 miles or 2 hours, a companion, and checked medicine labels [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Tired drivers pull over for a 15-to-20-minute nap, since rest beats every other remedy [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A02
Caffeine before a short nap doubles the benefit, and late-night driving invites fatigue [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A02
Distraction spans visual, manual, and cognitive kinds, from phones to food to passenger talk [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A02
Texting grips all three distraction channels, stealing eyes for 4.6 seconds or a football field at 55 mph and tripling crash risk on handheld tasks [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A02
Drivers silence phones, dodge heated talk, skip meals, and buckle kids and pets [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
Strong emotion clouds thought and attention, so the worried, excited, afraid, angry, or depressed drive poorly [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A03
The angry cool off with time, walks, or naps off-road, allow extra trip time, shrug off others' mistakes, never vent through the car, or let someone else drive [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A03
Aggressive driving deliberately endangers people or property through tailgating, darting lanes, and speeding, while road rage adds criminal violence or threats [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A03
Courteous driving prevents rage, and rage targets pull into lit public spots and call police without retaliating [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A03
Aging drivers seek evaluation after worried kin, lost familiar routes, warnings, recent violations or crashes, or doctors' orders, booking through the licensing medical board [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A04
Alcohol and impairing drugs touch about 40 percent of fatal crashes, and any amount raises crash odds [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A04
Under-21 purchase, possession, and drinking are illegal everywhere under zero-tolerance rules [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A04
Drink and drugs erode judgment, blur and slow vision from 0.02 BAC, dull color sense, and slow reactions, with impairment starting at sip one [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A04
Over-the-counter cold, allergy, nerve, and pep pills can sedate or agitate drivers, so labels get checked, doctors get asked, and alcohol never mixes in [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A05
Prescriptions like antidepressants, painkillers, sleep aids, and sedatives skew reflexes and judgment, so labels get checked and pharmacists get asked [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A05
Illegal drugs skew driving like alcohol, and a first drug-driving conviction within ten years brings $200 to $500 plus costs, 48 hours to 30 days in jail, and a 30-to-120-day suspension [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A05
DUI means 0.08 alcohol or any impairing influence, provable below 0.08, and 0.02 for drivers under 21 [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A05
Implied consent binds every operator to the arrest state's blood, breath, or urine tests, and refusal suspends the license, testifies in court, and doubles minimum jail on later convictions [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A05
Tested drivers may arrange their own blood test from a physician, nurse, phlebotomist, or technician [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A06
Suspended drivers may drive at once on an ignition interlock license with credit toward later requirements, arrestees get 10 to 15 minutes to reach an attorney, and private retests happen promptly at driver expense [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A06
A first alcohol conviction within ten years brings $200 to $500 plus costs, 48 hours to 30 days in jail, and a 4-to-6-month suspension, longer for minors, with worse later [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A06
Aggravation requiring jail means 30-plus over the limit, wrong-way highway driving, deadly crashes, .15 BAC within 2 hours, test refusal, or a passenger under 12 [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A06
DUI convicts surrender plates during suspension unless interlocked or hardship-licensed, and interlock devices bar driving above .02 breath alcohol [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0035]
